Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old male with history of anxiety presents with new onset severe left-sided headache, associated with mild photophobia, in setting of work-related stress; tension headache and migraine considered.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Awoke early morning (~5:30am) with severe, left-sided headache, described as "real kind of headachy feeling."  
- Onset: Abrupt, woke patient from sleep, began early morning (5:30am, earlier than usual waking time of 7:00am).
- Duration: Symptoms present since early morning, ongoing at time of consult.
- Nature/progression: Left-sided, more severe than prior headaches, which were previously milder and typically across the front of the head, not lateralized. No headache of this severity previously.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Slightly improved when lying down after initial discomfort; Paracetamol taken without significant effect.
- Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia (bright lights make eyes a bit sore but tolerable), early morning dizziness (resolved), no nausea, no neck stiffness, no fever.
- Previous history: Has had headaches before, less severe, not typically one-sided or posterior.
- Review of systems: No vomiting, no neck stiffness, no fever, no family history of migraine, no suicidal ideation, no recent changes in mood apart from frustration due to work stress.
- Pertinent negatives: No history of hypertension, never had BP checked, no smokers, no family history of significant physical illnesses.

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety (diagnosed ~2 years ago, ongoing, previously more significant; currently managed, some work-related stress, fluctuating frustration, no current severe symptoms).
- Medications:
  - Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Paracetamol (taken today for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented)
- No known drug allergies.
- No other chronic medical conditions or prior diagnoses mentioned.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- No smoking history.
- No alcohol or substance use mentioned.
- Pet cat at home.
- Regular exercise: Tries to run three times per week.
- Diet: Fair, not unhealthy, not particularly healthy.
- Work: Noted ongoing significant work-related stress (backlog, late nights), ongoing for "about a couple of months."
- No financial or detailed occupational/lifestyle concerns mentioned.

Family History:
- No family history of migraine or significant physical illness.
- Mother has a history of anxiety.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented (remote consultation).
- Vitals not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed or reported at this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Headache – possible tension-type headache versus migraine
  - Assessment: New onset severe, left-sided headache with photophobia and preceding work-related stress; previous headaches milder and non-lateralized; no red flag symptoms identified on review.
  - Plan:
    - Start Ibuprofen as first-line analgesia (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Continue Paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Maintain good hydration (1.5–2 L fluids/day excluding coffee/tea).
    - Ensure 7-8 hours of sleep nightly.
    - Review "danger signs" for headaches (link to be provided).
    - Arrange follow-up in 1 week; lower threshold for earlier re-contact if symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop.
    - Consider blood tests or further investigations if symptoms persist or worsen at follow-up.
- Issue 2: Work-related stress and anxiety
  - Assessment: Chronic anxiety, currently managed; increased recent stress and late nights due to backlog at work.
  - Plan:
    - Suggest considering a week off work to alleviate stress (self-certification discussed).
    - Refer/signpost to local counseling service (self-referral link to be provided).

General Plan:
- Provide summarized consult notes and patient information on danger signs.
- Book follow-up in one week; urgent re-evaluation if new concerning features arise.

Quality checks:

●	Missing elements:
  - Allergies documented as 'none known,' but no reconciliation for full drug/food/other allergies.
  - No physical exam due to remote consult—noted.
  - No medication reconciliation beyond those listed.
  - Vitals and neurological examination not performed/documented.
  - Mental status exam limited to discussion.
●	Internal conflicts:
  - None identified.
●	Transcript quality:
  - High quality, with clear chronology, symptom description, and pertinent negatives; no significant inaudible/noisy segments.
